Synopsis

@velora-dex/sdk 9.4.1 was published directly to npm with no matching source commit. Importing it fetched a macOS backdoor and registered launchctl persistence.

Story

The VeloraDEX compromise was registry-only. The attacker published `@velora-dex/sdk@9.4.1` to npm without changing the GitHub repository, so source review of the default branch would not show the payload.

The malicious delta was small. `package.json` carried the version bump, and `dist/index.js` gained three prepended lines. Those lines decoded and ran a shell command when application code imported the package.

The command downloaded `install.sh` from `89.36.224.5`. On macOS, the script created `~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.Terminal/`, selected an ARM64 or Intel `profiler` binary, made it executable, and registered it with `launchctl submit -l zsh.profiler`.

The attack did not depend on npm lifecycle hooks. `--ignore-scripts` would not stop it; the trigger was `require('@velora-dex/sdk')`. StepSecurity recommended pinning to 9.4.0 or earlier, removing the launchctl service and dropped binary, and rotating secrets from affected machines.
